title: Incremental Baseline Synthesizer & PR Gate for Token-Flow Regressions
creator: Priya Sharma
description: Problem: PRs occasionally introduce subtle throughput and p95 regressions that only show up under specific token-length mixes and KV-cache priming patterns. Current CI baselines are brittle: static snapshots are noisy and either cause false positives (flaky gating) or false negatives (missed regressions). Goal: build an incremental baseline synthesizer that continuously learns the active token-flow distribution, generates lightweight synthetic microworkloads for PR-level validation, and enforces a conservative CI gate that balances developer velocity against production safety. The feature should integrate into the PR pipeline, produce deterministic, reproducible microburst runs, and output human-readable evidence (traces + metrics) when a gate trips.
acceptance_criteria: Baseline recalibration reduces baseline mismatch to production median tokens/sec within 5% for three representative services (chat, completion, embeddings)
CI gate achieves >90% true-positive rate and <5% false-positive rate on our synthetic regression injection suite (1000 synthetic trials)
PR gate rendering includes: summary table (median tokens/sec, p95 latency, variance), time-series trace, and link to the reproducible workload artifact
Baseline updates are incremental (apply without full historic reprocessing) and complete within 3 minutes per model slice in CI run budget
Failing gates expose a remediation checklist and a one-click rerun to attach additional diagnostic traces
steps: Design: finalize baseline model representation (sliding-window quantiles + weighted token-length histogram)
Implement lightweight microworkload generator that can morph token-length mix and KV-cache priming patterns
Create bootstrapper job that runs nightly to seed baselines and a delta job that updates following each merged release
Add CI integration: PR pre-submit job that runs 3 short microburst trials against a candidate change and compares against baseline using a conservative test statistic
Instrumentation: capture tokens/sec, p95, tail distribution (p99.9), and sample traces; persist diagnostics to the PR artifacts store
Dashboard: Grafana panel for baseline drift, recent PR gate history, and lowest-confidence model slices
Alerting: add SLO on gate flapping and an ops runbook for suspected regression storms
progress_updates: 2026-02-16: Kickoff — scoped MVP to chat/completion models + single-region CI runner. Outcome: agreed on incremental baseline representation (quantile sketch + 7-bin token-length histogram).

2026-02-22: Prototype microworkload generator implemented. Uses sequence templates + synthetic user think-time. First runs showed stable median tokens/sec within noisy variance (seed sensitivity documented).

2026-02-28: Ran synthetic regression injection suite (delta +5%, +10% tokens/sec regressions). Early classifier flagged ~92% of injections but had ~8% false positives when network jitter simulated. Decided to add repeated-run consensus and bootstrap confidence intervals.

2026-03-05: CI integration spike complete — PR job runs as a lightweight Docker task. Proof-of-concept artifacts appear under PR attachments. Performance: ~2.5 minutes per trial in our small runner — within budget for short PRs.

2026-03-09: UX sync with PM and Console: we will include a compact summary card in PR and a detail link to Console traces. Decided to defer automatic rollback to a follow-up after further ops validation.
reviewer_feedback: Lina Ortega (SRE): prefer conservative thresholds and require 3-run consensus to reduce flakiness; include network emulation step in synthetic runner.
Daniel Cohen (Runtime): suggested adding KV-cache priming sequences captured from production traces to the morphing set — improves detection for cache-related regressions.
Aisha Patel (PM): request for an explainer paragraph in Console that ties gate failures to customer-facing risk (latency vs cost trade-offs).
Design review (2026-03-02): small table card accepted; recommended action: show delta percent and absolute token/sec delta, and include quick links to reproducer artifact.
